instructions.quote: Implement the work described by the user in the spec or tickets.
instructions.note: The assigned ticket plus its parent spec becomes the user's bounded implementation input.

instructions.quote: Use /tdd where possible, at pre-agreed seams.
instructions.note: Ticket and parent Testing Decisions supply the pre-agreed seams.

instructions.quote: Run typechecking regularly
instructions.note: The implementer retains the upstream typechecking cadence.

instructions.quote: single test files regularly
instructions.note: The implementer retains focused test execution during implementation.

instructions.quote: the full test suite once at the end.
instructions.note: The implementer runs the final suite; coordinator verification extends this after integration.

instructions.quote: Once done, use /code-review to review the work.
instructions.note: The workflow launches fresh independent reviewers after validating the implementer's candidate.

instructions.quote: Commit your work to the current branch.
instructions.note: Current branch means the assigned persistent issue branch in the assigned absolute worktree.

instructions.quote: read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists)
instructions.note: The implementer retains the domain-language context instruction.

instructions.quote: respect ADRs in the area you're touching.
instructions.note: The implementer retains the architecture-decision constraint.

instructions.quote: Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details.
instructions.note: Public behavior remains the test boundary.

instructions.quote: A good test reads like a specification
instructions.note: Behavioral, refactor-stable test quality remains unchanged.

instructions.quote: Tests live at seams, never against internals.
instructions.note: Tests remain attached to observable public seams.

instructions.quote: **Test only at pre-agreed seams.**
instructions.note: The ticket and parent spec must carry the pre-agreed seam.

instructions.quote: Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user.
instructions.note: A detached implementer consumes seams confirmed during specification and stops when they are absent or ambiguous.
instructions.rationale: Background ticket sessions cannot safely pause for an unplanned user design decision.

instructions.quote: **Implementation-coupled**
instructions.note: Implementation-coupled tests remain prohibited.

instructions.quote: **Tautological**
instructions.note: Expected results must retain an independent source of truth.

instructions.quote: **Horizontal slicing**
instructions.note: The implementer works in vertical tracer-bullet slices.

instructions.quote: **Red before green.**
instructions.note: A failing test precedes minimal implementation with no speculative features.

instructions.quote: **One slice at a time.**
instructions.note: Each cycle remains one seam, one test, and one minimal implementation.

instructions.quote: **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage
instructions.note: The implementer never refactors inside red → green. Review may identify changes that a later remediation implementer performs; that remediation path is a workflow extension, not delegation of the TDD-loop rule.

instructions.quote: Every section applies on every cycle — consult them before and during the loop, not after.
instructions.note: The implementer receives the complete TDD contract before work and applies it throughout every cycle.

instructions.quote: See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.
instructions.note: Both referenced support documents are embedded byte-exact in the implementer role.

instructions.quote: Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?"
instructions.note: The ticket and parent spec must answer the seam question before detached implementation begins.
instructions.rationale: Background ticket sessions cannot safely pause for an unplanned user design decision.

instructions.quote: Tests behavior users/callers care about
instructions.note: Tests retain a user- or caller-observable purpose.

instructions.quote: Uses public API only
instructions.note: Tests remain restricted to public APIs.

instructions.quote: Survives internal refactors
instructions.note: Tests should not fail on behavior-preserving internal changes.

instructions.quote: Describes WHAT, not HOW
instructions.note: Test names and assertions describe behavior rather than implementation.

instructions.quote: One logical assertion per test
instructions.note: Each test retains one logical assertion.

instructions.quote: Mocking internal collaborators
instructions.note: Internal collaborators are not mocked.

instructions.quote: Testing private methods
instructions.note: Private methods are not direct test seams.

instructions.quote: Asserting on call counts/order
instructions.note: Call counts and internal call order remain prohibited assertions.

instructions.quote: Test breaks when refactoring without behavior change
instructions.note: Behavior-preserving refactors must not invalidate tests.

instructions.quote: Test name describes HOW not WHAT
instructions.note: Implementation-shaped test names remain a red flag.

instructions.quote: Verifying through external means instead of interface
instructions.note: Verification proceeds through the product interface, not a side channel.

instructions.quote: Expected value restates the implementation
instructions.note: Expected values retain an independent, known source of truth.

instructions.quote: **Integration-style**: Test through real interfaces, not mocks of internal parts.
instructions.note: Tests remain integration-style through real public interfaces.

instructions.quote: External APIs (payment, email, etc.)
instructions.note: External APIs remain valid mock boundaries.

instructions.quote: Databases (sometimes - prefer test DB)
instructions.note: Database mocking retains the upstream test-database preference.

instructions.quote: Time/randomness
instructions.note: Time and randomness remain system-boundary mock candidates.

instructions.quote: File system (sometimes)
instructions.note: Filesystem mocking retains the upstream boundary caveat.

instructions.quote: Your own classes/modules
instructions.note: Owned classes and modules remain non-mock boundaries.

instructions.quote: Internal collaborators
instructions.note: Internal collaborators remain non-mock boundaries.

instructions.quote: Anything you control
instructions.note: Controllable internal dependencies are not mocked.

instructions.quote: Pass external dependencies in rather than creating them internally:
instructions.note: Boundary dependencies retain the dependency-injection design rule.

instructions.quote: Create specific functions for each external operation instead of one generic function with conditional logic:
instructions.note: External boundaries retain the SDK-style, operation-specific interface rule.

instructions.quote: Mock at **system boundaries** only:
instructions.note: The governing mock rule remains restricted to system boundaries.

instructions.quote: At system boundaries, design interfaces that are easy to mock:
instructions.note: Boundary interface design must support simple, behavior-focused test doubles.

instructions.quote: Each mock returns one specific shape
instructions.note: SDK-style boundary mocks retain one specific return shape.

instructions.quote: No conditional logic in test setup
instructions.note: SDK-style boundary mocks avoid conditional setup logic.

instructions.quote: Easier to see which endpoints a test exercises
instructions.note: Operation-specific interfaces keep exercised endpoints visible.

instructions.quote: Type safety per endpoint
instructions.note: Operation-specific boundary interfaces retain endpoint-level type safety.

instructions.quote: Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:
instructions.note: Every candidate receives separate Standards and Spec evaluation.

instructions.quote: Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.
instructions.note: The outer workflow owns parallel isolated sessions; the final reporter owns aggregation.

instructions.quote: The issue tracker should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.
instructions.note: Tracker operations are a bootstrap prerequisite; the workflow holds instead of installing or configuring another skill.
instructions.rationale: A background implementation run lacks authority to mutate the user's skill configuration.

instructions.quote: Whatever the user said is the fixed point
instructions.note: Coordinator-owned durable Git state supplies the ticket or parent fixed point.

instructions.quote: If they didn't specify one, ask for it.
instructions.note: The workflow derives an exact fixed point or stops; detached reviewers never ask mid-run.
instructions.rationale: A resumable graph needs one durable fixed point rather than conversational input per reviewer.

instructions.quote: Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD`
instructions.note: Read-only coordinator validation captures the exact three-dot command before review.

instructions.quote: Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.
instructions.note: Read-only coordinator validation captures and validates every commit-list line.

instructions.quote: confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`)
instructions.note: Coordinator validation resolves the exact base SHA before review.

instructions.quote: A bad ref or empty diff should fail here
instructions.note: Candidate validation fails before review when the ref or diff is invalid.

instructions.quote: Issue references in the commit messages
instructions.note: Bootstrap uses the explicit parent reference and its tracker graph instead of commit-message discovery order.
instructions.rationale: The command's parent argument is the authoritative scope boundary.

instructions.quote: A path the user passed as an argument.
instructions.note: A parent path passed to `/implement-tickets` is accepted as the authoritative parent source.

instructions.quote: A PRD/spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
instructions.note: Bootstrap resolves the explicit parent and scoped tracker relationships rather than guessing from branch names.
instructions.rationale: Heuristic branch-name matching is too ambiguous for automated graph mutation.

instructions.quote: If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is.
instructions.note: Missing or ambiguous specification data produces a safe bootstrap hold.
instructions.rationale: Detached execution cannot safely block on an unplanned conversation.

instructions.quote: If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".
instructions.note: Both ticket-level review axes are mandatory before integration.
instructions.rationale: Automated integration without an originating Spec axis would weaken acceptance.

instructions.quote: Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written
instructions.note: Coordinator validation discovers canonical standards paths; the Standards role reads and applies them.

instructions.quote: the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below
instructions.note: The complete baseline is embedded in every Standards role.

instructions.quote: **The repo overrides.**
instructions.note: Documented repository standards continue to override baseline smells.

instructions.quote: **Always a judgement call.**
instructions.note: Baseline smells remain labelled heuristics rather than hard violations.

instructions.quote: skip anything tooling already enforces.
instructions.note: The Standards reviewer does not duplicate tooling-enforced findings.

instructions.quote: Send a single message with two `Agent` tool calls.
instructions.note: The outer workflow launches both agents in one `parallel()` stage.
instructions.rationale: pi-dynamic-workflows, not an inner reviewer, owns parallel execution.

instructions.quote: Use the `general-purpose` subagent for both.
instructions.note: Named least-privilege Standards and Spec agent types replace general-purpose reviewers.
instructions.rationale: Named roles bind read-only tools, axis prompts, model routing, and isolation.

instructions.quote: The full diff command and commit list.
instructions.note: Both reviewers receive the validated command and complete commit list.

instructions.quote: The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full
instructions.note: Validated standards paths enter as data; the complete baseline is embedded verbatim in the role.

instructions.quote: every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule)
instructions.note: Standards findings retain per-file or per-hunk citations to documented rules.

instructions.quote: any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk.
instructions.note: Baseline findings retain the smell name and changed hunk evidence.

instructions.quote: Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls
instructions.note: Documented breaches and heuristic smells remain distinct.

instructions.quote: Skip anything tooling enforces.
instructions.note: The Standards brief retains its explicit tooling deduplication rule.

instructions.quote: Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls — documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.
instructions.note: Schema and runtime checks enforce a non-empty 1–400-word Standards report.

instructions.quote: requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial
instructions.note: Spec review retains missing and partial requirement detection.

instructions.quote: behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep)
instructions.note: Spec review retains scope-creep detection.

instructions.quote: requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong
instructions.note: Spec review retains incorrect-implementation detection.

instructions.quote: Quote the spec line for each finding.
instructions.note: Every Spec finding retains direct source evidence.

instructions.quote: Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.
instructions.note: Schema and runtime checks enforce a non-empty 1–400-word Spec report.

instructions.quote: If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.
instructions.note: The graph cannot integrate a candidate without a complete Spec review.
instructions.rationale: A mandatory parent and ticket spec is part of the workflow's acceptance boundary.

instructions.quote: Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned.
instructions.note: Ticket evidence and final output preserve the original reports under separate headings.

instructions.quote: Do **not** merge or rerank findings
instructions.note: Structured gating consumes both axes without combining their meaning or priority.

instructions.quote: End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_
instructions.note: Final aggregation retains per-axis counts and worst finding without selecting one overall winner.

instructions.quote: Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.
instructions.note: Integration and reporting continue to require independent Standards and Spec outcomes.

instructions.quote: The path or fetched contents of the spec.
instructions.note: The workflow supplies exact ticket and parent references; the Spec reviewer reads their full contents and linked evidence.

instructions.quote: **Standards** — does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
instructions.note: The Standards axis retains its original question.

instructions.quote: **Spec** — does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / PRD / spec?
instructions.note: The Spec axis retains its original question.

instructions.quote: Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:
instructions.note: The Standards reviewer applies each full smell definition and remedy to the actual diff.

instructions.quote: The diff command and commit list.
instructions.note: The Spec reviewer receives the validated diff command and complete commit list.

instructions.quote: **Mysterious Name** — a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
instructions.note: The complete Mysterious Name definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Duplicated Code** — the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
instructions.note: The complete Duplicated Code definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Feature Envy** — a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
instructions.note: The complete Feature Envy definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Data Clumps** — the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
instructions.note: The complete Data Clumps definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Primitive Obsession** — a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
instructions.note: The complete Primitive Obsession definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Repeated Switches** — the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
instructions.note: The complete Repeated Switches definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Shotgun Surgery** — one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
instructions.note: The complete Shotgun Surgery definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Divergent Change** — one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
instructions.note: The complete Divergent Change definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Speculative Generality** — abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
instructions.note: The complete Speculative Generality definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Message Chains** — long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
instructions.note: The complete Message Chains definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Middle Man** — a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
instructions.note: The complete Middle Man definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.

instructions.quote: **Refused Bequest** — a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.
instructions.note: The complete Refused Bequest definition and remedy remain in the Standards baseline.
